The *Pañcaṅguliyattheraapadāna* is a biographical poem preserved within the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. It commemorates the verses and karmic past-life deeds of the elder (thera) Pañcaṅguliya [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral indexes translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread internal Pali reuse, identifying 73 matching passages across 32 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest overlap is with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), particularly between segments §3.1–4.4 of this text and §1281–1284 of the commentary [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits standard stock verse sharing with several other Therāpadāna poems, most notably *Padumapūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 132, §3.1–9.1 matching §7.1–13.1), *Gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 131), and *Kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 205) [DharmaNexus].
